transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-11-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Garcia (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Security Eng), Emma Walters (Northbridge CISO), Ravi Patel (Head of Platform), Sofia Martinez (SecOps)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Alex ran through the external pen test items, we talked remediation and timelines. Customer asked about KMS, RBAC, audit logs, and patch cadence. Agreed to share full artifacts and schedule follow-up.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick security review focused on the recent pen test results and our vulnerability management approach. Priya and Jordan are with me from the SE/security side.
[00:12] Emma: Great, thanks. We had a quick read of the summary but wanted to go deeper on the high/critical findings and the timelines for fixes. Also high level, how you integrate with our SSO and KMS.
[00:25] Priya: Sure, we'll cover the vulnerabilities, where they were found (mostly in the hosted control plane and a small set of infra misconfigs the tester flagged), and remediation status. Quick note, the pen test was a third-party external test from Q4, scope = hosted API + onboarding console + audit logs.
[00:45] Ravi: When you say \"hosted control plane\" can you be specific — I'm trying to map to our network diagrams, like VPC peering and the dedicated pools.
[00:55] Jordan: Yes, the findings largely touched on some ephemeral infra components — misconfigured IAM roles in the provisioning workflow and an outdated library pinned in an internal admin service. Nothing in the model runtime sandbox, the testers couldn't get into the KV cache or model state. Sorry, they said KV cash in their notes which was odd.
[01:15] Emma: OK that's helpful. Can you run through critical items and status? We have compliance windows for SOC 2 evidence next quarter.
[01:23] Alex: Absolutely. High-level: 3 criticals, 6 high, rest medium/low. The three criticals were: 1) an admin endpoint with weak auth that allowed an escalation path (now behind stricter RBAC + rate limit), 2) an outdated dependency with a remote code exec CVE — patched and rolled in canary, 3) misconfigured S3 bucket with object ACLs — fixed and re-scanned.
[01:48] Sofia: For the RCE patch, do you have an ETA for full rollout to prod and the rollback plan? We need to update our change control and maintenance windows.
[01:58] Priya: The RCE patch is in canary across 10% of traffic; full rollout scheduled this week pending canary metrics. Rollback is automated via our deployment orchestration, and we keep immutable artifacts so revert is straightforward. We'll provide the deployment runbook.
[02:18] Ravi: What about the patching cadence for underlying infra — kernel/security patches, base OS images — how often do you do that, and how do you communicate windows to customers?
[02:28] Jordan: We do monthly OS/image patching for managed hosts, with critical hotfixes applied out-of-band. For Dedicated customers we support scheduled maintenance windows and can align patching cadence. For hosted customers we aim to minimize disruptions and publish maintenance notices in the console and via email.
[02:48] Emma: Is there a public dashboard for CVE status or a feed we can subscribe to?
[02:52] Alex: Not a public dashboard yet; we can provide a CVE digest and vulnerability tracker export for customers with enterprise agreements — we'll share that as part of the remediation artifacts.
[03:05] Sofia: On encryption, we want to confirm key management: where are keys stored, do you allow customer-managed keys (CMKs) and how are they rotated?
[03:15] Priya: We support Redwood-managed KMS keys for hosted customers and offer customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private deployments. Keys are stored in cloud KMS with HSM backing for the BYOK flow; rotation policies exist and we can share the rotation schedule. We use envelope encryption for data at rest and TLS 1.2+/1.3 for transit.
[03:40] Emma: For audit logs and retention, our policy is 7 years for certain financial artifacts — can you retain logs that long and provide tamper-evident storage?
[03:51] Jordan: We can retain logs for extended periods as an add-on; logs can be exported to customer-owned S3 buckets or a SIEM via forwarding. We also have append-only storage options and signed log exports for tamper evidence. There are costs associated with long-term retention which we'll outline.
[04:12] Ravi: On RBAC/SSO, we will need SAML or OIDC and fine-grained role mapping — can you map to our internal groups and integrate with our SCIM?
[04:22] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning is supported for enterprise accounts to sync groups. Role mapping is configurable and you can build custom roles; we'll share the RBAC matrix doc.
[04:35] Emma: How are audit trails generated for admin actions — do you log token-level detail and can you link actions back to SSO identity?
[04:44] Jordan: We capture token-level events for control plane actions and correlate with SSO identities when SSO is enabled. The console exposes an audit export and we can push to customer SIEM with enriched fields.
[04:58] Emma: Regarding secure SDLC, do you run dependency scanning, SCA, static analysis, and do you have a process for triage and CVE scoring?
[05:10] Alex: Yes — we run SCA on all repos, static analysis on critical services, and use a priority matrix for triage. Jordan manages the security on-call and the runbook describes triage times: criticals within 24 hours, high within 72 hours, etc.
[05:30] Sofia: Who owns the patch verification and who does the final sign-off for production deploys after a security fix?
[05:39] Priya: For infra fixes it's our infra ops + security lead. For application libs we use CI gates; a security reviewer sign-off is required for high/critical fixes before prod rollout.
[05:50] Emma: Are you SOC 2 Type II ready? We need evidence and timelines.
[05:55] Alex: We're currently in the remediation phase post-controls review; the target for SOC 2 Type II audit completion is Q2 2026. We can share interim evidence packages and the SOC 2 readiness report.
[06:08] Ravi: Can you provide the pen test raw artifacts — I want to feed them into our risk mgmt system.
[06:14] Alex: Yes, we'll share the full pen test PDF, issue tracker, and a remediation mapping sheet. We'll redact PII where needed.
[06:23] Emma: For vulnerability management, do you use an external tracker (JIRA) and can you grant us read-only access to the tickets that affect our tenancy?
[06:32] Jordan: We can provide scoped read-only views or an export per customer; for Dedicated we often grant a shared ticket view.
[06:40] Sofia: A couple of nitty-gritty questions: patch windows are typically overnight PST for us, do you offer timezone alignment?
[06:49] Priya: For Dedicated yes; for hosted we schedule low-traffic windows and can discuss alignment for enterprise customers.
[06:57] Emma: Any lingering gaps identified from the pen test that are still open?
[07:02] Alex: Two high items remain: a rate-limit hardening on an admin API (in progress) and a dependency in a third-party lib that needs a patch but awaits upstream release; we have a mitigation in place. We'll include ETA columns in the tracker.
[07:18] Ravi: What about the SDLC for infra as code, do you sign commits and require MR reviews?
[07:26] Jordan: We have mandatory code review policies, CI gating, and Terraform plans are validated in preview environments. We also run drift detection.
[07:36] Emma: How do you handle emergency patches that touch customer data planes? Are customers notified in advance or post-fact?
[07:45] Alex: For critical hotfixes that could affect data plane availability we send pre-notice when possible; for zero-day emergency mitigations we notify as soon as practical and provide a post-mortem. We try to limit customer impact and we have playbooks for communication.
[07:59] Sofia: On data residency — our legal requires EU-only processing for certain workloads. How do you prove the region and that logs/extracts don't cross borders?
[08:09] Priya: We can restrict workloads to EU regions, disable cross-region replication for those tenants, and provide region-specific export endpoints. We'll also provide attestation language for contracts.
[08:22] Emma: The testers mentioned some confusion around \"KV cache\" naming — we just want to confirm sensitive state never leaves the tenant VPC.
[08:30] Jordan: Correct, model KV and state are kept in tenant-isolated storage for Dedicated/Private; for hosted, ephemeral caches are isolated per tenant and we don't persist secrets. We'll clarify the naming mismatch in the pen test notes.
[08:47] Ravi: Do you have a demonstrated patch verification or test harness we can run to validate fixes?
[08:53] Priya: We can run regression suites and share the test harness results for critical fixes; we also run fuzzing for some inputs.
[09:03] Emma: OK let's talk timeline and next steps.
[09:07] Alex: Action items: we'll send the full pen-test artifacts and remediation tracker; Priya will annotate the architecture for KMS and audit log flows; Jordan will share the vulnerability management runbook and CVE triage SLAs. We'll set a follow-up technical deep dive to walk through the tracker and the patching schedule — propose 2025-11-25.
[09:32] Sofia: That works. Please include the SOC 2 readiness package in the materials.
[09:36] Alex: Will do. Any final questions?
[09:40] Emma: No more on my side. Appreciate the thoroughness.
[09:44] Ravi: Thanks everyone.
[09:46] Alex: Thanks all, we'll circle back with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the follow-up.

Recap (auto): Share pen test PDF + remediation tracker; architecture diagram with KMS/dataflow; vulnerability mgmt runbook; schedule follow-up on 2025-11-25.

End of transcript.
